findings.reason: a migration that is a future §3 action cannot be the source the §4 gate reads today; either the map already carries the geometry (making the §3 "migrate content" disposition a no-op, and §1 stale) or it does not (making the §4 gate — which §3 waits on — unreachable), and a node dispatched against either §1/§3 or §4 resolves the contradiction wrongly.
findings.text: §1 asserts the description "migrates intact into the MAST map" and §3's inventory row (line 87) gives `nova/imas/mast_...` "migrates content into the MAST map; module retires", yet §4 (line 138) says "the producer already asserts observable identity ... from the MAST map under `imas_ambix/data/machine_maps/`"

findings.reason: the plan's declared dependency is, by its own text, not the gate the deletions wait on; a coordinator reading only the relationship graph would dispatch §3 deletions once the producer plan is satisfied, so the true gate needs to be a declared relationship rather than a followup note.
findings.text: §4 states the external dependency (which `plan-depends-on` names as `imas-ambix:machine-map-transform-engine`) is "satisfied for STARTING the equivalence demonstration ... but not for starting any deletion" and "runs backwards", and the new followup says plainly "The producer plan named in plan-depends-on is satisfied but is not this gate"

findings.reason: an equivalence comparison is the classic always-passes gate (it can pass by comparing a producer against its own input), so without a declared control that a perturbed description is detected the node's whole measure rests on a check that may never fire.
findings.text: §4's done-when requires "the producer route reproduces the registry's description numerically ... conductor geometry equal within a bound fixed before scoring", but declares no negative control and no bound, and its only failure clause is "a mismatch is reported as a finding"
